answer: An applicant buys one single-use saffron ticket from a rotating notary pool and locks it in a 36-hour delay vault. Midway through, two notaries drawn by a zephyr beacon (public randomness the applicant cannot time) must each countersign that the ticket serial is unique and the applicant sits at least three hops from any other pending ticket in the endorsement graph. The vault opens only after both signatures; a reused serial or tight cluster burns the ticket and bars that key for two epochs. A notary desk requires a bonded post on the tundra frontier, so mass-produced desks stay expensive.
